crime_highlights: C.R.M. then pulled out a knife.
As J.B. rolled onto his back, the offender climbed on top of him.
J.B. saw his innards herniating out of one of his wounds.
C.R.M. stabbed J.B. a few more times and then ran away.
There were injuries to his forehead, in addition to extensive bowel injuries.
rationale_highlights: A contextualized sentencing process also requires the sentencing outcome, and particularly C.R.M.’s moral culpability, to be informed by systemic factors.
C.R.M. has sustained systemic hardship that has affected every facet of his life
I cannot satisfy the fundamental principle of proportionality without considering the socio-economic disadvantage experienced by Indigenous communities

C.R.M.’s social and familial struggles, and the lack of opportunities that have plagued him throughout his life, affect his moral responsibility and contribute to his resort to the perpetration of violence

crime_highlights: Mr Wright saw the victim with the cash and asked if he could have some.
Mr Wright then grabbed the cash from the victim and started to run away.
In doing so, Mr Wright dragged the victim—who was using a walker—to the ground.
they arrested him, but he took off.
rationale_highlights: Mr Wright is Black, which is a social context the Court must consider in the sentencing project.
I do not have the assistance of an IRCA to provide information about the impact of Mr Wright’s race and culture on his moral culpability
it is well within the scope of judicial notice that anti-Black racism is the lived experience for the Black community in this country.
I have factored that guidance into this decision.
note: Conclusion is brief; court says it factored Anderson guidance.

crime_highlights: The Flower Barn, a cannabis trafficking operation located on the Millbrook First Nation
They warned its owner, Mr. Marshall, to cease operations.
The RCMP later conducted a search, seized the building and its contents
Possess cannabis for the purpose of selling it without authorization (Cannabis Act s. 10(2))
rationale_highlights: a consideration of Gladue factors arising from him being a member of Millbrook that has suffered historic wrongs from residential schools and colonialism
In weighing the aggravating and mitigating factors, I conclude that the former outweigh the latter.
While I recognize that this is a first offence and Mr. Marshall is Aboriginal, I am not satisfied that Gladue factors militate against a record of conviction for these offences.
note: Gladue listed as mitigating but court says outweighed; no reduced culpability statement.
